# Story 13.2: Execute the critical review and record file-referenced recommendations

Status: review

## Story

As a user (Dave),
I want the finished codebase reviewed against the plan from Story 13.1 with actionable recommendations written up,
So that I have a prioritized list of what to improve now that feature work is essentially complete.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each aspect named in the Epic prose is reviewed against the codebase and produces concrete, file-referenced recommendations (not generic advice) recorded in that aspect's section of `/.github/epic-descriptions/epics-9999-99-99.md`: Tailwind usage; readability/maintainability (naming conventions, code organization, clarity/terseness, best practices); consistency of coding style and conventions; error handling & logging; security implications & vulnerabilities; test coverage & quality; dependencies & third-party libraries usage; documentation & comments; opportunities for refactoring & optimization.
2. The finalized document at `/.github/epic-descriptions/epics-9999-99-99.md` contains the review plan (from Story 13.1) plus per-aspect recommendations, and no source file, RED/GREEN unit test, or e2e test is created or modified by this story.

## Tasks / Subtasks

- [x] Task 1: Review each aspect; record file-referenced recommendations (AC: #1)
  - [x] 1.1 Tailwind usage — flag inconsistent/ineffective class use and custom styles that should be minimized.
  - [x] 1.2 Readability & maintainability — naming conventions, code organization, clarity/terseness, best-practice adherence; cite specific files/functions.
  - [x] 1.3 Style consistency — inconsistencies in coding style/conventions across the four projects.
  - [x] 1.4 Error handling & logging — gaps or inconsistent patterns (note: `no-console` is a hard lint rule here — recommend compliant logging, not raw `console.*`).
  - [x] 1.5 Security implications & vulnerabilities — auth/cookie/CSP surface (AD-5), input validation, dependency risks.
  - [x] 1.6 Test coverage & quality — weak or missing critical-path coverage; tie in with Epic 12's findings where relevant.
  - [x] 1.7 Dependencies & third-party libraries — outdated/unused/redundant deps (deps are root-hoisted for `dms-material`).
  - [x] 1.8 Documentation & comments — missing or stale docs/comments on critical paths.
  - [x] 1.9 Refactoring & optimization opportunities — concrete, prioritized candidates with file references.
- [x] Task 2: Finalize the document (AC: #2)
  - [x] 2.1 Confirm `/.github/epic-descriptions/epics-9999-99-99.md` contains the review plan followed by per-aspect recommendations, each recommendation referencing the specific file(s)/path(s) it applies to; prioritize so Dave can act on the highest-value items first.
  - [x] 2.2 Confirm no source file, unit test, or e2e test was created or modified — this Epic produces only the document.

## Dev Notes

- **This Epic is review-only.** Per the prose: "This epic does not require the standard set of RED/GREEN Unit tests nor the e2e tests." There is no TDD triple here — two stories that together produce one recommendations document. Do NOT add or modify any source/test code; only write `/.github/epic-descriptions/epics-9999-99-99.md`.
- **Depends on Story 13.1:** the plan and per-aspect section headings already exist in `/.github/epic-descriptions/epics-9999-99-99.md` — fill them in place; do not restructure the document.
- **Recommendations must be concrete.** Each finding should name the file(s) and (where useful) line range, state the problem, and give a specific recommendation — not generic "improve readability" advice. Prioritize so Dave can act on the highest-value items first.
- **Consult the spines as reference:** ADs/FRs in `.github/workflow-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/**/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md` and `prds/**/prd.md` give intended design to compare actual code against — useful for the structure/pattern/security aspects.
- **Project-specific gotchas worth checking during review (verify current state before recommending):** Electron CSP inline-script handling in packaged builds, root-hoisted deps for `dms-material`, the `no-console` hard lint rule, and the shared e2e SQLite DB reuse behavior.

### Project Structure Notes

## Dev Agent Record

### Agent Model Used

Qwen Code CLI (headless execute-story run) — orchestrator + one sequential sub-agent per task. Review-only story: no code was written, so the "tasks" were read-and-record passes over each aspect rather than red/green test cycles.

### Debug Log References

- No build/test/lint commands are applicable to this review-only story (no source or test files touched). Verification is by inspection of the produced document and `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`.
- Document completeness check: all nine aspect sections present in `.github/epic-descriptions/epics-9999-99-99.md` (Aspects 1–8 each carry file-referenced findings; Aspect 9 is the consolidated P0/P1/P2 prioritized action list).
- Review-only confirmation: `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` lists only `.github/epic-descriptions/epics-9999-99-99.md` and the two epic-13 story files — no `.ts`/`.js`/`.mjs`/`.json` source or test file was created or modified.

### Completion Notes List

- Task 1 (AC #1): Reviewed each of the nine aspects named in the Epic prose against the actual codebase and recorded concrete, file-referenced recommendations into that aspect's section of `.github/epic-descriptions/epics-9999-99-99.md`. Each finding names specific file(s) with line ranges where useful, states the problem, and gives a specific fix — not generic advice.
  - Aspect 1 (Tailwind): two parallel theming systems (`--dms-*` tokens vs Material SCSS), dead custom utility classes in `apps/dms-material/src/styles.scss`.
  - Aspect 2 (readability/maintainability): naming-convention drift, oversized route files (e.g. `universe/index.ts`), duplicated logic; cited specific functions/files.
  - Aspect 3 (style consistency): mixed error-response styles and file-naming suffixes across the four projects.
  - Aspect 4 (error handling & logging): catch-and-swallow patterns, a settings schema/handler field-name mismatch that silently drops `tax_free_income`, generic unlogged 500s; recommended compliant structured-logger usage per the `no-console` hard rule.
  - Aspect 5 (security): packaged Electron server defaults to `NODE_ENV=development` so auth/CSRF are skipped in shipped builds; CSRF stored-token comparison never performed; set-secure-cookie endpoint plants unverified tokens.
  - Aspect 6 (test coverage & quality): weak `toBeDefined()` error assertions, e2e shared-DB isolation leaks with fixed sleeps.
  - Aspect 7 (dependencies): ~8 unused direct deps in the root-hoisted manifest plus a stray `apps/electron/package-lock.json`.
  - Aspect 8 (documentation): stale/contradictory electron README build section, drifted `env.example` and e2e test counts, no server API documentation.
  - Aspect 9 (refactoring & optimization): consolidated the cross-cutting findings into a prioritized P0/P1/P2 action list with effort/risk/value per item so Dave can act on the highest-value items first.
- Task 2 (AC #2): Confirmed `.github/epic-descriptions/epics-9999-99-99.md` contains Story 13.1's review plan at the top followed by all nine per-aspect recommendation sections, each referencing specific file(s)/path(s), prioritized for actionability.
- Task 2 (AC #2): Confirmed no source file, unit test, or e2e test was created or modified — this Epic produces only the document (verified via `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`).
